_about: PROPOSAL for the owner's approval, not established anywhere. Combined-candidate review and visible failed hand-offs (owner-approved development-process correction, 2026-11-24). Each item supersedes the standing TEST entry it names and keeps its placement. Establishing these words is the owner's act (tools/establish_governance.py --decisions docs/governance/combined-review-2026-11-24.json, dry run first). The DAY-TO-DAY application is later, only after code promotion, and uses the same successor bodies with the DAY-TO-DAY supersession ids stated in application_plan.
approved: wording owner-approved; establishment remains the owner's act
occasion: Combined-candidate review and unrecorded hand-off reliability, 2026-11-24

TEST.when: after approval, by an explicit owner establishment action

DAY-TO-DAY.when: later, after the supporting code is promoted and verified

application_plan.constraint: No new competing Discipline or Workflow is established.

body.about: A software change carried through a CLI, MARS and Git, from a recorded request to merged, tested, pushed and recorded work

activities.done_when: The carrier can say which Conversation carries the work and what governs it.
activities.what: Call orient, then recall with the work described, for the Conversation carrying it; read what governs it, the Workflows and Disciplines recall points to, and the outstanding work (work_overview).

activities.done_when: The request is in the record and its expectation id is known.
activities.what: Record the work as a request in that Conversation (record_request), with what would show it is done.

activities.done_when: The parts, their dependencies and seams, each part's to-do list, difficulty, required capabilities and checkable done-when, and whether the combined candidate warrants review are written where the workers can read them; any exceptional earlier specialist or contract review is named.
activities.what: Write a brief plan: the parts, which are independent and which depend on which, and the seams they share (who owns each shared file or interface). For each part give its hand-off (as for implement), its difficulty and the capabilities it requires. State whether the combined candidate warrants independent review because of its risk or complexity; routine localised changes need none. Name an earlier specialist or contract review only for a security or authority boundary, an irreversible change, a foundational interface, or a dependency choice whose late discovery would cause major rework. For a hands-on iteration the plan also names the smallest coherent candidate: which parts make a usable first preview. Set each part's difficulty from the part itself; routine parts are not given frontier difficulty. The plan is the hand-offs and the seams the parts share, not a specification of each part's internals: what a Builder can settle within its own part is left to it. Small, localised work is planned by the carrier in a line or two; small corrections get no separate specification round.

who.role: a Planner, or the carrier itself for small, localised work

activities.done_when: Any exceptional earlier specialist or contract review has one verdict and findings, the accepted findings are folded in and checked by the carrier, or the plan records that the step is skipped.
activities.what: Skip plan review by default. Use one earlier specialist or contract review only for a security or authority boundary, an irreversible change, a foundational interface, or a dependency choice whose late discovery would cause major rework. Its author folds in one findings set and the carrier checks the revision against those findings. It is not reviewed again unless the owner changes the requirements or a finding leaves an architectural decision unresolved.

who.role: an Independent Reviewer, not the plan's author

activities.done_when: Each part is committed on its branch, its targeted tests finished in the run that returns it, and anything incomplete or unverified is stated.
activities.what: Delegate independent parts concurrently, subject to available runtime capacity and dependencies. Give each worker a bounded, executable assignment with clear ownership and completion criteria. Each works in its part's checkout on its part's branch, named as `repository`, started through MARS or by hand; it claims the checkout for its run and returns to the carrier with the checkout and branch. A part whose result can be acted on alone (reviewed, corrected, or handed to a part that depends only on it) is delegated with resume_on_return, so its return resumes the carrier while other parts still run; parts are left to join only when the next step needs all of them. Each hand-off is a short to-do list the worker can carry without replanning: goal; the part's checkout and branch (the same ones its earlier rounds used); ordered steps, ending with commit, then the targeted tests run in the foreground to completion, then commit any fixes; the files it owns; what is out of scope; checkable done-when; what to return. Delegate it with the part's difficulty and required capabilities; name a runtime only when the owner did. Continuations and corrections keep the part's difficulty. For a hands-on iteration the hand-off's checks are focused: the tests of what the part changes and its seams, and browser checks in the owner's browser only -- no full suites, other browser engines, repeated reruns or screenshots unless the request asks for them. Each worker gets this activity's Discipline and the Builder Persona.

who.role: a worker for each independent part

activities.done_when: Every finished compatible part is merged, or is recorded as not merged and why; the integrated candidate's test commands and counts are recorded, and where people use the change its real rendered interface has been inspected on the product path.
activities.what: In a hands-on iteration, integrate the finished, compatible parts as soon as they form a coherent candidate; parts still running land in a later candidate if the owner wants them. Merge each finished branch into the work's branch with git merge, resolving conflicts with the authors' reports in hand; commit work a read-only sandbox could not. When integration is delegated rather than done by the carrier, it is delegated with this activity (then review when warranted, correct, and verify), not implement, to one integrator. Immediately after integration and before independent review, run the integrated targeted checks for everything changed and the execution-boundary tests when dispatch or mentis.execution changed. Where people use the change through an interface, inspect the real mounted product path -- navigation, state, permissions and the backend it calls -- at this point. Record what fails; a candidate with a blocking failure does not advance to review.

who.role: the carrier, integrating, or one integrator it delegates

activities.done_when: When review is warranted, the combined candidate has one independent verdict and one consolidated findings set, each finding carrying its evidence, severity and owning part or integration seam; otherwise the plan records why routine localised work needs none.
activities.what: When the plan says risk or complexity warrants it, after integration one independent reviewer or tester reviews the exact combined candidate against the whole request, including cross-component seams and the rendered real product path where people use the change, and returns one consolidated findings set. Routine localised changes need no independent review. Do not repeat each Builder's self-tests as separate acceptance reviews. A specialist may review an earlier slice only for an exception named in the plan: a security or authority boundary, an irreversible change, a foundational interface, or a dependency that could cause major rework. Run on a runtime other than the author's, with review_of naming the request being reviewed and `repository` the workstream's review checkout, never the author's; the reviewer checks out the exact commit under review there (or the carrier puts it there first, when the reviewer's runtime cannot write Git metadata) and confirms it. For a change a person uses through an interface, review the real mounted product path -- navigation, state, permissions and the backend it calls -- before spending rounds on synthetic harnesses: they check focused regressions, and their passing is not evidence that the interface works. Individual parts are not reviewed separately before integration except for a named specialist exception. Attribute each finding to the part it belongs to, or to the integration when it lies in a seam between parts. Mark each finding blocking, not blocking, or out of scope (outside the authorized request: separate work needing its own authorization). A blocking finding names the requirement it violates and how to reproduce it. Blocking: it loses or corrupts data, breaks essential navigation, prevents normal use or a working build, breaches authority or security, or leaves out something the request requires. Everything else -- a cosmetic or minor visual issue, a small deviation, a test-only problem, a latent risk with no present path -- is not blocking. In a hands-on iteration, the combined candidate receives independent review only when its risk or complexity warrants it; routine localised changes need none, and the owner's hands-on evaluation is not split into per-part acceptance reviews.

who.role: an Independent Reviewer, not the author

activities.done_when: Blocking findings are assigned once to their owning Builders or integrator in parallel where practical and are fixed or recorded as not fixed and why; nonblocking and out-of-scope findings are recorded as follow-up work; the corrected integrated candidate receives focused verification of the corrections and what they touch. A genuine remaining blocking defect is still fixed; no review count is a reason to accept defective work.
activities.what: Each part's blocking findings go back to that part's author, all parts at once, each as a short to-do list as for implement; findings in a seam go to the integrator. Focused verification checks the integrated corrections and what they touch, not the whole review again; a genuine remaining blocking defect is still fixed, and no review count is a reason to accept defective work. Before correcting, the author names the invariant each finding breaks and checks the other paths that could break it the same way, and the correction covers them, in the part's own checkout and branch. A correction is bounded to its findings and shown by the targeted tests that check them; it never reopens planning. Focused verification that finds another path of the same invariant sends it back with the invariant named. Verification is not dispatched again when nothing it would check has changed. A blocking finding that is not fixed is said, with why. Findings that are not blocking, and out-of-scope findings, are recorded as discovered work, not corrected in this request -- the carrier does not turn one into a correction unless the owner widens the request or another governing requirement makes it blocking, and does not add acceptance criteria after building began -- and a finding the owner has deferred or dismissed is neither corrected nor raised again.

who.role: the part's author; focused verification goes to the independent reviewer or tester

activities.done_when: The focused verification commands and their counts are recorded, and every correction and what it touches holds or a genuine remaining blocking defect is named for correction.
activities.what: After corrections are integrated, perform focused verification of each correction and what it touches. Do not repeat the whole combined-candidate review or unaffected test scope. A genuine remaining blocking defect is still fixed; no review count is a reason to accept defective work. If there were no blocking corrections, retain the integrated checks and early real-interface inspection already recorded. For a hands-on iteration, leave the accepted candidate running through the existing preview or test process, started detached from the run so that it outlives it, and have the carrier open its address and check that it answers and shows the affected interactions. Launch instructions are not a preview. Where a preview cannot be left running, say that plainly and do not claim the deliverable met. For a release, run any additional full regression, cross-browser or platform checks the release calls for.

who.role: the carrier, integrating, or the integrator it delegated

activities.done_when: The result is pushed, the outcome is recorded, and merged workspaces are removed.
activities.what: For a hands-on iteration, commit the candidate on its own branch and report it with the address it is running at, checked after starting it, what it includes, what is unfinished and its known non-blocking issues; merging it into main and pushing waits for the owner's acceptance or a release. For a release, commit and push the integrated result; record_outcome on the request with what was done and what remains, and when its deliverable is met, say so: further work the owner approves after that is a new request continuing this one, with its own done-when, not carried under this one; record a durable lesson separately with record_material, the outcome Turn as its basis; remove merged workspaces and branches with git branch -d. WORKSPACES ARE RETIRED WHEN THEY HAVE SERVED THEIR PURPOSE, not only when the work ends: before a checkout is retired its branch is pushed to a provisional branch (wip/<work>/<part>) -- preservation, not acceptance, merge or deployment; nothing goes to main, test/integration or a release branch without the owner's authority, and reviewer experiments are not pushed (their evidence is recorded instead). A superseded checkout or a finished review checkout is retired once its commits are on a remote branch and its evidence is recorded, and only when no live lease holds it, nothing in it is uncommitted, and no other checkout links into it; anything else is kept and reported. A review checkout has no branch of its own: once its verdicts and evidence are recorded and the commits it reviewed are on a remote branch, it is retired when that combined-candidate review and any focused verification using it are complete. Review findings that were not fixed are recorded as discovered work.

decisions: Applying a change to the day-to-day Brain, or deploying it
Pursuing discovered work the request's follow-up permission does not cover
Merging a hands-on iteration candidate into main
body.done_when: A hands-on iteration: a committed candidate is running and reachable at an address the carrier checked, its focused checks are recorded, and the outcome says what it includes, what is unfinished and its known non-blocking issues, and which checkouts it leaves and why. A release: the change is merged and pushed, the targeted tests pass on the result, every review finding is fixed or recorded as discovered work, and the outcome is recorded with what remains.
body.evidence: The pushed commit id; the test commands with their passed, failed, skipped and error counts; for each review held, its verdict and findings and which were fixed; the request's expectation and its recorded outcome; any lesson, recorded with that outcome as its basis. For an iteration, the address the candidate is running at and when it was checked.
body.interrupted: Unfinished work stays where it is and is reported, never deleted: each workspace with uncommitted changes, stashes or unpushed commits is named with its path, its branch and what is unfinished, as what remains in record_outcome. A later session continues it by orienting, reading the request and its outcome (recall, work_overview) and taking up the named branches; work handed to an agent is continued by addressing it again with the recorded context.
body.name: Software change
body.text: Orient and recall what applies, record the request, plan the parts, build independent parts in parallel on their standing branches and have each Builder self-test its work, integrate the finished compatible parts into one isolated development candidate, run the integrated checks and, where people use the change, inspect the real rendered interface early, obtain one independent combined-candidate review when risk or complexity warrants it (routine localised changes need none), send its blocking findings to the relevant Builders or integrator in parallel where practical, correct and integrate them, perform focused verification of the corrected candidate, then integrate accepted work into cumulative TEST for the owner's evaluation and record the outcome with what remains and, separately, any lesson. The carrier coordinates; a Builder implements. Owner-only decisions are those listed here and those the request reserves to the owner. Before asking one, the carrier checks the request and the owner's recorded decisions: what they already answer is decided, and authority already granted is not asked for again. A new owner-only question is asked when it arises, once, and work that does not depend on its answer goes on meanwhile; what it decides waits for the answer. Each request has one of two purposes, read from the owner's words. A hands-on iteration -- the owner asks to build something to test, try an idea, get a working candidate, or wrap up for a preview -- aims at a usable candidate in the owner's hands promptly: a brief plan, independent parts in parallel, focused tests of what changed and its seams, then the smallest coherent candidate integrated, built and smoke-checked on the main affected interactions in the browser the owner tests in (Windows Chrome or Edge unless the request names another), left running through the existing preview or test process at an address the carrier has opened and checked, with non-blocking defects recorded; then the carrier stops for the owner's evaluation. A production release -- only when the owner explicitly asks for release, production readiness or deployment -- adds the full applicable regression, cross-browser and platform verification, independent review with correction of release blockers, release preparation and the owner's deployment approval. When the purpose is unclear it is an iteration, and an iteration never turns into release work by itself. A candidate that loses data, breaks essential navigation or does not build is not offered. A preview is a running, reachable preview: a built candidate and instructions for starting it are not one. The owner's latest instruction about work governs it. A follow-up reaches the carrier as a resumption, or in place of a delegation it was about to make; the carrier reconciles it before issuing anything further: it starts nothing the instruction no longer needs, keeps completed work, does not build on running parts it no longer needs and reports them as superseded, and says what is kept, stopped and still running. Work the instruction does not touch continues. WORKSPACES CARRY ON. Each part has one checkout and one branch, named in its hand-off and given as `repository` -- a directory named this way must already exist, so the carrier prepares the checkout (or delegates preparing it) before naming it; its corrections, continuations and resumed runs are delegated to the same checkout and branch, whichever run, runtime or model carries them. A second checkout for a part is made only for concurrent work on it that cannot share one. Each workstream has one review checkout, separate from every author's checkout, reused round after round (`review_of` with `repository`); concurrent reviews get one each. When the carrier cannot tell that a checkout is safe to reuse -- a live lease, changes nobody accounts for -- it settles that before delegating rather than letting a new clone be made. A HAND-OFF THAT TIMES OUT may still have happened: the carrier reads the record for it (history, work_overview) before anything else, retries only with the same operation key and the same repository after waiting, and never starts a second agent for work already running; a hand-off it still cannot confirm is reported as unconfirmed, with its key, not as work not done. An authorized hand-off that fails before it is recorded must be retried once with the same operation key or reported as a failed hand-off with the remaining work named; it is never reported as done or as a deliberate stop. One carrier coordinates one objective: a follow-up asked as a new request is handed to the work it is about (attach_follow_up), and there is never a second integration, preview or completion report beside the first. Independent review follows complexity, foundational impact and the cost of finding a defect later: routine styling, simple filters and localised changes need none; complex changes, shared APIs, governance, execution, security and foundational changes warrant it, and a plan is reviewed before building when its risk justifies it. This is judged in words, not scored, and is not a loop every change goes through. A correction is re-reviewed for what it changes and what that touches, not by repeating the whole review. Nothing moves from one activity to the next by itself, and how far the work has got is read from the record and from Git.

How coordinated work is organised. The coordinator sets the scope, shared interfaces, contracts and integration approach first. Builders implement independent parts in parallel where practical, each on its own standing part branch, and self-test what they change. Compatible finished parts are integrated into one isolated development candidate, its integrated tests are run, and where people use the change its real rendered interface is inspected early. Integration assembles and preserves the work; it is not acceptance, release authorization or deployment authorization. Independent review follows risk and complexity: routine, localised changes need none; when the risk or complexity warrants it, one independent reviewer or tester evaluates the combined candidate against the request, including cross-component seams and the rendered product path, and returns one consolidated findings set. Individual parts are not reviewed separately before integration; an earlier specialist or contract review is used only where security, authority, irreversible changes, foundational interfaces or dependency risks warrant it. Blocking findings go to the relevant builders or the integrator, in parallel where practical; nonblocking and out-of-scope findings become follow-up work, not correction rounds. Corrections are integrated and receive focused verification of what they change and what that touches, not a repeat of the whole review; a genuine remaining blocking defect is still fixed, and no review count is a reason to accept defective work. Accepted work is integrated into the cumulative TEST integration branch for the owner's evaluation. Nothing is retried automatically: a failed part is reassigned or finished by the integrator, and the report says which.
